column1: # Kaburagi, Kato, Fukuda and Taguchi (2021), "Control of the vocal tract when experienced saxophonists perform normal
# notes and overtones", Acoust. Sci. & Tech. 42(2):83-92, doi:10.1250/ast.42.83, Figs. 4 (participant A) and 5
# (participant B). Two professional saxophonists, 3-D MRI while sounding a saxophone mouthpiece on a uniform vinyl tube
# of 18 cm (short) or 28 cm (long), not a saxophone body; low = normal technique, mid and high = overtones. Area
# [cm^2] perpendicular to the centre line, 40 equal sections, section 1 = glottis end, section 40 = mouthpiece edge
# (the figures' abscissa "from the glottis to the mouthpiece"). Read off the PDF's vector paths (40 points per curve),
# each panel's axes calibrated on its own tick marks and labels (largest label-fit residual 7.91e-4 cm^2; points on
# sections 1..40 within 0.0017); values to the plot's precision, not the MRI's. Tract length [cm], Table 1, in column
# (long tube, mid note), B 0.24 cm^2 and 0.30 cm (short tube, mid note).
